html-table-processing: none

A tabular overview of the examples. Click on an example to open its page.

<!-- The table is generated by example_table.py from the linked examples and
     the features listed in the front matter of each example page. -->

```{=html}
<style>
/* styles.css lays every page out as 200px sidebar | content | 200px margin,
   with !important. This page keeps the sidebar but drops the margin column,
   so that the table gets its width; the extra body in the selectors outranks
   styles.css. Quarto places some elements, such as the page navigation at
   the bottom, by named column lines, so the tracks carry those names --
   without them the browser appends implicit columns for these elements,
   which take width away from the table. Below 992px the sidebar is folded
   into a menu and Quarto's own layout applies. */
@media (min-width: 992px) {
  body #quarto-content.page-columns {
    grid-template-columns:
      [screen-start screen-start-inset page-start page-start-inset body-start-outset] 200px
      [body-start body-content-start] minmax(0, 1fr)
      [body-content-end body-end body-end-outset page-end-inset page-end screen-end-inset screen-end] !important;
  }
  body #quarto-margin-sidebar { display: none !important; }
  /* Without the margin column the content would run up to the window edge. */
  body #quarto-content main.content { padding-right: 1.5em; }
}
</style>
```
